To access the homepage of the WikiDoc scholar program, you can click on the provided link. To begin editing a page, you need to click on the edit source button located at the top of the page. Editing WikiDoc articles differs from using a standard word processor. Instead of a what you see is what you get (WYSIWYG) approach, WikiDoc employs text codes to create specific page elements, such as headings. This coding system is referred to as Wikitext or Wiki-markup, and it is designed to facilitate editing. Once you click edit source, you can start entering or modifying text on the page. The table provided in the documentation shows examples of what to type in the editing space to achieve the desired formatting. Why Use Specific Formatting with Equal Signs for Sections and Subsections? Using equal signs to create sections, subsections, and sub-subsections allows WikiDoc to automatically generate a table of contents for the page. If you only use bold text for headings, an automatic table of contents will not be created. Examples of Basic Formatting This page provides guidance on how to perform basic text formatting on WikiDoc pages. Bold and Italics To make text bold, you can use three apostrophes on each side of the text. For example: `'''This is bold text'''` will appear as: This is bold text To italicize text, use two apostrophes on each side of the text. For example: `''This is italicized text''` will appear as: This is italicized text You can combine bold and italics by using five apostrophes. For example: `'''''This is bold and italicized'''''` will appear as: This is bold and italicized If you need to display multiple apostrophes or tildes without them being interpreted as formatting, you can use the `` tag. For example: `'''''without bold italics'''''` will display as: '''''without bold italics''''' Quotation Formatting To place text in quotes and indent it with large quotation marks, you can use specific formatting codes. Font Color To change the font color, you can use the `` tag. For example: `your text` will display as: your text in red. You can also use hexadecimal color codes. For example: `your text` will display as: your text in a custom hexadecimal color. Font Size Font sizes range from 1 to 7, with the default size being 3. To change the font size, use the `` tag. For example: `your text` will display as: your text in a larger font size. To increase the font size by one level above the default, use: `your text` To decrease the font size by one level below the default, use: `your text` Font Typeface To change the font typeface, use the `` tag. For example: `your text` will display as: your text in the Courier font. Signatures Users can leave timestamped signatures to identify themselves. Typing three tildes (`~~~`) will insert the user's name. Typing four tildes (`~~~~`) will insert the user's name along with a timestamp. Typing five tildes (`~~~~~`) will insert only a timestamp. For example: `~~~` will display as: C Michael Gibson talk `~~~~` will display as: C Michael Gibson talk 14:23, 10 March 2006 (GMT) `~~~~~` will display as: 14:23, 10 March 2006 (GMT) Signatures should always be used on talk pages. Line Breaks Paragraphs in Wikitext are created by leaving a blank line between them. If two lines of text are written without a blank line in between, they will appear on the same line. To force a line break without creating a new paragraph, you can use the `
` tag, though this is rarely necessary. Horizontal Lines To create a horizontal line, type four dashes (`-`) on a separate line. For example: `-` will display as: Alternatively, you can use the XHTML code `
` to create a horizontal line. Note that the largest two section headers automatically generate a horizontal line below the heading title. HTML and XHTML Tags Background HTML is a language used to create web pages. However, it is now considered deprecated by the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) and is strongly discouraged. XHTML is a revised version of HTML that addresses issues within the original HTML standard. Compatibility and Future-Proofing Older browsers rarely encounter issues with XHTML, but the same cannot be said for HTML. The flaws in the original HTML specifications often led to misinterpretation. WikiDoc strongly prefers wikimarkup over HTML or XHTML for future-proofing purposes. Since HTML is deprecated, it is possible that future browsers may no longer support it. Wikimarkup, which can be considered a shorthand version of XHTML, is expected to evolve alongside XML standards. Therefore, it is recommended to use wikimarkup whenever possible instead of HTML or XHTML. The `` tag is specifically intended for program source code. `` or ``: These tags apply a strikethrough effect to text. ``: This tag underlines text. ``: This tag displays text in small caps. `` and ``: These tags create superscript and subscript text, respectively. `
